newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso slides on pent-up dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso slides on pent-up dollar demand.

text.p: The Philippine peso skidded on Wednesday on pent-up demand for dollars by importers, traders said.
The peso ended at 29 to the dollar from 28.50, with the central bank a dominant seller at 29 pesos, traders said.
One trader estimated the central bank may have sold more than 80 percent of the total market volume of $73.1 million.
"It's the import season. The central bank has to sell dollars if it wants the currency to stabilise," a trader said.
Traders said the central bank's limited intervention in the past week had bottled up dollar demand.
